drug_name: Multivitamin with Iron (Vitamin C, Vitamin D, Vitamin E, Vitamin B6, Folate, Vitamin B12, Iron)
what_its_for: These vitamins and minerals work together to support your overall health. Vitamin C helps your immune system and heals wounds. Vitamin D keeps your bones and teeth strong and supports your immune system. Vitamin E protects your cells from damage. Vitamin B6 helps your brain work properly and supports your immune system. Folate (Folic Acid) helps your body make new cells and is especially important during pregnancy to prevent birth defects. Vitamin B12 keeps your nerves and blood cells healthy and helps prevent a type of anemia. Iron helps your red blood cells carry oxygen throughout your body and prevents iron-deficiency anemia.
how_to_take: Take this supplement by mouth, usually once a day or as directed by your doctor or pharmacist. Swallow tablets or capsules whole with a full glass of water (8 ounces). To reduce stomach upset and to help your body absorb iron best, take it with a meal or snack. If you are taking chewable tablets, chew them completely before swallowing. Do not crush, chew, or break extended-release capsules or tablets unless your pharmacist tells you it is safe to do so.
dosing: The usual adult dose is one tablet or capsule once daily, or as directed on the product label or by your healthcare provider. Do not take more than the recommended amount listed on the label unless your doctor tells you to. Children's doses are different — always use a product made for your child's age group and follow the dosing instructions on the package. Pregnant or breastfeeding women may need a specially formulated prenatal vitamin — ask your doctor or pharmacist which product is right for you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next regular dose. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Since vitamins and minerals build up in your body over time, missing an occasional dose is usually not a serious problem, but try to take it at the same time each day to build a good habit.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture — do not store in the bathroom medicine cabinet or near the kitchen sink. Keep the container tightly closed. Keep all vitamins and supplements out of the reach of children — iron overdose can be very dangerous and even life-threatening in young children. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the label. If the tablets change color, smell unusual, or crumble easily, discard them and get a new supply.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking your multivitamin with iron at the same time as antacids, calcium supplements, or dairy products, as these can reduce how well your body absorbs iron — try to space them at least 2 hours apart. Avoid drinking coffee, tea, or cola within 1 hour of taking iron, as they can also reduce absorption. Do not take more than the recommended dose, as too much iron, Vitamin D, or Vitamin E can be harmful. Avoid taking multiple vitamin or supplement products at the same time without checking with your pharmacist, as this can lead to getting too much of certain nutrients. If you smoke, talk to your doctor before taking high-dose Vitamin E or beta-carotene supplements, as high doses may be harmful for smokers.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get medical help right away if you or your child accidentally takes too much — especially if a child swallows iron tablets, as this is a medical emergency. Call your doctor if you have severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting after taking this supplement. Contact your doctor if your stools turn very dark or black (a small amount of darkening is normal with iron). Call your doctor if you develop signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also talk to your doctor if you notice no improvement in your symptoms after several weeks, or if your symptoms get worse.
when_it_works: Vitamins and minerals work gradually over time. You may start to feel more energy and less fatigue within a few weeks of taking iron and B vitamins regularly if you were deficient. Vitamin D and bone-related benefits may take several months to show up in blood tests or bone density measurements. Folate's protective effects during pregnancy begin right away, which is why it is important to start taking it before you become pregnant or as early in pregnancy as possible. For the best results, take your supplement every day as directed and maintain a healthy, balanced diet.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women: A prenatal vitamin with folate (at least 400–800 mcg) and iron is strongly recommended. Ask your doctor which prenatal vitamin is best for you. Starting folate before pregnancy is ideal to prevent neural tube birth defects. Children: Use only products designed for children and follow age-appropriate dosing. Keep iron supplements safely away from children, as overdose is a medical emergency. Older adults (65+): May need higher amounts of Vitamin D and Vitamin B12, as absorption decreases with age. Talk to your doctor about whether your current supplement meets your needs. People with certain health conditions: If you have kidney disease, liver disease, hemochromatosis (iron overload disorder), or certain blood disorders, talk to your doctor before taking iron or high-dose vitamins, as some nutrients can be harmful in large amounts. People taking medications: Certain medicines (such as antibiotics, blood thinners like warfarin, levodopa for Parkinson's disease, or seizure medications) can interact with vitamins and iron. Always tell your doctor and pharmacist about all supplements you take.
